title: Alumina Cooler
model_title: Rotary Alumina Cooler (Indirect, External Water-Spray Cooling)

introduction.definition: A rotary alumina cooler is a slowly rotating drum whose outside is sprayed with water. Hot alumina tumbles inside and is cooled through the steel shell, never touching the water.

temperature.title: Indirect cooling through the shell
temperature.description: Hot alumina tumbles inside while water sprays and runs over the outside of the shell, removing heat through the steel wall (no contact between water and product). Lifters improve contact with the cooled wall. Shell temperature differences and scaling of the external surface reduce performance.

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Cooler — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Alumina Cooler.
A rotary alumina cooler is a slowly rotating drum whose outside is sprayed with water.
Hot alumina tumbles inside and is cooled through the steel shell, never touching the water.
Typical applications include cooling calcined alumina (rotary kiln plants); cooling other hot bulk solids.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Cooler Drum: Shell with Liners / Lifters (rotates), Cooler Drum: Riding Tyres & Girth Gear (turn with the shell), Inlet Hood (hot alumina feed) & Discharge Hood.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Cooler — Operation

script.narration: How the Alumina Cooler works.
Hot alumina enters the drum.
The drum rotates and tumbles it.
Sprays cool the shell.
Cooled alumina discharges.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Hot alumina tumbles inside while water sprays and runs over the outside of the shell, removing heat through the steel wall (no contact between water and product).

video_tutorials.title: Alumina Cooler — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Alumina Cooler.
Check spray pattern and temperatures.
Roller and tyre inspection.
Shell inspection; descale exterior.
Watch for shell scaling: hot product. Common cause: hard water.
Watch for tyre wear: noise. Common cause: misalignment.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
